draft_board_observations.source: completed startup draft board, 3 screenshots, 12 teams x ~30 rounds
draft_board_observations.dst: No DST picks spotted anywhere on the board. IDP likewise absent. Those two look genuinely unused.
draft_board_observations.qb_count_approx: ~52 QBs drafted (22 + ~16 + ~14 across the three screenshots). APPROXIMATE -- hand-counted off dense screenshots, +/- several.
draft_board_observations.verdict: Model overestimates QB consumption by roughly 55%. Direction of the positional_bench_appetite diagnosis is CONFIRMED; magnitude is less extreme than feared.
draft_board_observations.kicker_picks_are_placeholders: RESOLVED by the user: kickers on this board are stand-ins for future ROOKIE PICKS, a standard dynasty-startup workaround for interfaces that can't draft future picks. They are NOT kicker selections and must be discarded as players. This confirms the original 'no K/DEF/IDP slots' reading -- the board contradicted it only superficially.
draft_board_observations.data_quality_trap: A placeholder pick is structurally IDENTICAL to a real one: same position field, same pick slot. Nothing in a draft feed distinguishes them. Naive ingestion of this board would conclude the room drafted ~36 kickers and calibrate positional consumption on it. Any future backtest that reads real draft boards needs a guard.
draft_board_observations.proposed_guard: Position-agnostic and already derivable from data the engine holds: a pick at a position the league has ZERO starter demand for cannot be a real roster selection, so exclude it from expected_positional_consumption's observed-share counts. Uses starter_slot_counts, names no position, and would have discarded all ~36 automatically.
draft_board_observations.qb_verdict_unaffected: ~52 actual vs 80.6 predicted is a QB-to-QB comparison, untouched by the placeholder issue. Placeholders only shrink the denominator: ~324 real player picks rather than ~360. Feeding the model the smaller number lowers its QB estimate to roughly 75 -- still far above 52, so the positional_bench_appetite bug stands confirmed.

rookie_draft.KEY_FINDING: Rookie-draft consumption tracks ROOKIE CLASS SUPPLY, not roster demand. WR took 22 of 48 picks (46%) while this league starts only 2 WR + flex. No starter_slot_counts-derived model can reproduce that, so fixing the TAXI-has-no-demand bug would NOT be enough -- a rookie draft needs a different consumption model entirely, driven by which rookies exist, not by what rosters need.
rookie_draft.SECOND_FINDING: 42 of 48 picks were traded before use. Draft-order/roster-id assumptions from a startup do not carry over.

rookie_consensus_validation.hypothesis: User: rookie positioning is so heavily and uniformly researched that rookie consensus is a far better benchmark than veteran ADP.
rookie_consensus_validation.source_used: KeepTradeCut's own rookie flag + rank, ALREADY in data/baseline/external. 64 flagged rookies. No external ADP fetch needed.

order_test.context: Higher than every vendor-vs-vendor agreement measured this session (CBS/FP DST 0.885, DS/FP kickers 0.727, CBS/DS DST 0.587).

composition_test.CAVEAT: Largely ENTAILED by the order result, not independent evidence: a room taking 45 of the top 64 in near-consensus order will reproduce the pool's composition almost by construction. The order correlation is the real finding.

rookie_consensus_validation.implication: The rookie-draft consumption model I said was missing is buildable from data already held. Rookie drafts should key consumption to the rookie POOL (composition + consensus order), not to starter_slot_counts. This is a genuinely different code path from the veteran/startup case, which is what the evidence supports.
rookie_consensus_validation.LIMITS: ONE draft, ONE rookie class, ONE league. rho 0.908 could be a strong-consensus class (2026 WR-heavy) rather than a general law. Needs replication across leagues and ideally a second class before any constant is calibrated to it.
